25-014.r: PAC → reports to Speaker, presented in Lok Sabha (copy laid in Rajya Sabha); max 22 members: 15 from Lok Sabha + up to 7 from Rajya Sabha.
25-014.t: Don't flip the split: 15 members come from Lok Sabha, only 7 from Rajya Sabha.

25-015.r: PAC → formed every year, not more than 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha); examines CAG audit report and reports to Parliament.

25-016.r: PAC submits its report to the Speaker of Lok Sabha → presented in Lok Sabha; members: 15 (Lok Sabha) + 07 (Rajya Sabha) = 22.
25-016.h: PAC formula 15 + 07 = 22; the bigger share and the report both go to Lok Sabha.

25-019.r: PAC → examines CAG report and scrutinises appropriation and finance accounts of Government; has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS), not '25 Lok Sabha members'.

25-020.r: Chairman of PAC → appointed by Speaker of Lok Sabha from among its members; till 1966-67 from ruling party, since 1967-68 an opposition member.

25-021.r: Public Accounts Committee → Financial Committee; Committee on Petitions → Functional Committee; Joint Committee on Stock Market Scam → Ad hoc; Departmental Committees → Standing.

25-022.r: Estimates Committee (first 1950) → 30 members, all from Lok Sabha, no Rajya Sabha member; PAC and Public Undertakings Committee → 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).
25-022.t: Don't confuse Estimates Committee (30, Lok Sabha only) with PAC (22, both Houses).

25-025.r: Financial Committees (3) → Estimates, Public Accounts, Public Undertakings; Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs is a Housekeeping Committee.
25-025.t: Salaries and Allowances committee deals with money but is Housekeeping, not Financial.

25-026.r: Three Financial Committees of Parliament → Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, Committee on Public Undertakings.
25-026.h: PEP: Public Accounts, Estimates, Public Undertakings.
hi: Committee on Public Undertakings (सार्वजनिक उपक्रम समिति)

25-027.r: CAG audit report → examined by Public Accounts Committee; Committee on Public Undertakings also examines CAG reports, so book accepts (a) and (c).

25-028.r: Parliamentary committees → Standing and Ad hoc; three main Standing Committees: Estimates, Public Accounts, Public Undertakings; 17 Department-related Standing Committees came in 1993.
25-028.c: All four are standing committees, so none fits. The book wrongly calls the SC/ST Welfare Committee a department-related standing committee; it is a separate standing committee of Parliament.

25-029.r: Lok Sabha Ethics Committee → initially ad hoc; cannot take up sub-judice matters; complaints not limited to Lok Sabha members. First Ethics Committee: Rajya Sabha, 1997.

25-030.r: Parliamentary Committees exist on Public Undertakings, Government Assurances (tracks ministers' promises) and Estimates; none on Welfare of Minorities.

25-031.r: Department-related Standing Committees: Social Justice & Empowerment, Urban Development, Labour → under Lok Sabha; Health and Family Welfare → under Rajya Sabha.

25-032.r: Consultative Committees of MPs for Railway Zones → constituted by Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs; MPs of the respective zones are members.
25-032.t: Not the Ministry of Railways, even though the committees are for railway zones.

25-033.r: 18th Lok Sabha committees 2024-25 (Speaker Om Birla): PAC → K.C. Venugopal; Estimates → Sanjay Jaiswal; Public Undertakings → Baijayant Panda (so 'Estimates – Panda' is wrong).

25-034.r: 2G spectrum Joint Parliamentary Committee (2011) → 30 MPs: 20 from Lok Sabha + 10 from Rajya Sabha.

25-035.r: 2G Scam Joint Parliamentary Committee → headed by P.C. Chacko; report given to Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar.

25-036.r: Committee on Subordinate Legislation → checks whether Executive properly uses delegated power to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws.
25-036.t: Don't confuse with Committee on Government Assurances, which checks ministers' promises made on the floor of the House.

25-037.r: Committee on Subordinate Legislation → delegated rule-making by Executive; exists in both Houses, 15 members each, nominated by Speaker/Chairman; ministers cannot be members.
25-037.t: The official name is 'Subordinate' Legislation, not 'Delegated', 'Executive' or 'Administrative' Legislation.

25-038.r: Independent regulators (telecom, insurance, electricity) → reviewed by Parliament's ad hoc committees and Department-related Standing Committees (24); not Finance Commission, FSLRC or NITI Aayog.

26-001.r: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act → enacted 1954; came into effect 1 June 1955.

26-002.r: Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955, Section 15 → all offences are cognizable and summarily triable.

26-003.r: PCR Act 1955 offences → tried by Judicial Magistrate First Class (special courts); in UP, Chief Judicial Magistrate/Judicial Magistrate courts are designated Special Courts.

26-004.r: PCR Act 1955 → all offences are cognizable, triable summarily and non-compoundable.

26-005.r: PCR Act 1955 → Section 15(1): all offences cognizable; Section 10A(1): State Government can impose collective fine; punishment is imprisonment and fine.

26-006.r: PCR Act 1955, Section 5 → refusing admission to hospital, dispensary or educational institution on ground of untouchability; jail one to six months plus fine.

26-007.r: PCR Act 1955, Section 10A → power of State Government to impose collective fine.

26-008.r: Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 → Section 1(2): extends to the whole of India.

26-009.r: PCR Act 1955 → punishes preaching and practice of untouchability and enforcing any disability from it; extends to whole of India (Section 1(2)).

26-010.r: PCR Act 1955: Section 14 → offences by companies; Section 10 → abetment (public servant neglecting investigation); Section 12 → presumption by courts.

26-011.r: PCR Act 1955, offence by a company → person in charge of its affairs (Director, Manager or Secretary) deemed guilty and punished.

26-012.r: PCR Act 1955, Section 12 → court presumes act was on ground of untouchability when victim is a member of a Scheduled Caste.
26-012.t: Presumption covers Scheduled Castes only, not Scheduled Tribes.

26-013.r: Untouchability is not an offence when the accused and the victim belong to the same social group.

26-014.r: PCR Act 1955, Section 12 → court can presume 'untouchability' motive when offence is against a member of the Scheduled Castes (unless contrary proved).

26-015.r: PCR Act 1955, Section 14A → protection of action taken in good faith (no suit against Central or State Government).

26-016.r: PCR Rules 1977 at Centre → Ministry of Home Affairs, Social Justice & Empowerment and Tribal Affairs (not Minority Affairs); main responsibility with States/UTs.

26-017.r: Women's reservation in urban local bodies → 74th Amendment, not 73rd. Hindu Marriage Act 1955; Hindu Succession Act 1956; Sati (Prevention) Act 1987.
26-017.t: Don't confuse 73rd with 74th Amendment: urban local bodies come under the 74th.

26-018.r: Indian High Court Act → 1861; Indian Divorce Act → 1869; Royal Title Act → 1876; Indian Arms Act → 1878.

26-019.r: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 → came into force on 26 October 2006.
26-019.t: Act year 2005, but in force from 2006.

26-020.r: MISA (Maintenance of Internal Security Act, 1971; repealed 1977) → security law, not a social Act; Anti-Dowry, PCR, Immoral Traffic Acts are social Acts.

26-021.r: Criminal Tribes Act → first enacted 1871 by the British; first in northern India, later extended to Bengal.

26-022.r: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → President's assent 11 September 1989; came into force 30 January 1990.
26-022.t: Act year is 1989, but it came into force in 1990.

26-024.r: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → has 23 Sections.

26-025.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 23(1) → Central Government makes rules by notification in the Official Gazette.

26-026.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → 'economic boycott' defined in Section 2(bc).

26-027.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989 → public servant committing an offence under Section 3 → minimum one year imprisonment.

26-028.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989: Section 14 → Special Court and Exclusive Special Court for speedy trial; Section 15 → Special Public Prosecutor.

26-029.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act, Section 14 → State Government, with concurrence of Chief Justice of High Court, notifies a Court of Session as Special Court for each district.

26-030.r: Court of Session made Special Court under SC/ST Atrocities Act (Section 14) → purpose: speedy trial.

26-031.r: Appeal under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → lies to the High Court on both facts and law.

26-032.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → based on Doctrine of Protective Discrimination; implements the system under Article 15(4).

26-033.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Section 16 → State Government imposes and realises collective fine.
26-033.t: Not the District Magistrate or Special Court; the power is with the State Government.

26-034.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989, Section 8 → court may presume abetment, common intention and common object.

26-035.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989, Section 6 → applies certain Indian Penal Code provisions (e.g. Sections 34, 149); IPC now replaced by Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

26-036.r: SC/ST Atrocities Rules, 1995 → investigating officer to finish investigation within thirty days and report to Superintendent of Police; rule changed by Amendment Rules, 2016.
26-036.c: MPPSC's key gave (d) 30 days, the 1995 rule; the 2016 amendment replaced it with a sixty-day limit for investigation plus charge-sheet, so the book marks none.

26-037.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 → anticipatory bail is barred.

26-038.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act, 1989, Section 18 → anticipatory bail (Section 438) does not apply to arrests under this Act.

26-039.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act offences → investigated by police officer not below Deputy Superintendent rank (Central rules of 1995).

26-040.r: Special Court (SC/ST Atrocities Act) can forfeit convict's property, remove suspect from area, take measurements/photographs; cannot authorise a non-police person for extra investigation.

26-041.r: Special Court (SC/ST Atrocities Act) → can remove a person, forfeit property, take measurements; cannot impose collective fine.

26-042.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act applies only to accused who are not SC/ST; its Section 6 applies the IPC's general exceptions (Chapter IV), such as private defence. MPPSC gave bonus marks.
26-042.c: The book says the accused cannot plead (a) or (c), but Section 6 of the Act applies the IPC's general exceptions, which include private defence and slight harm; MPPSC gave bonus marks.

26-043.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act → non-SC/ST person harming SC/ST member on allegation of witchcraft → jail six months to five years, plus fine.

26-044.r: SC/ST Atrocities Act: 'Exclusive Special Court' → Section 2(1)(bd), not 2(d); 'Victim' → 2(ec); 'Dependent' → 2(bb); offences are by non-SC/ST persons.

26-045.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995, Rule 17 → District Level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee, set up by District Magistrate in each district.

26-046.r: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995, Rule 18 → 'Material for Annual Report'.

26-047.r: RTI Act → passed Lok Sabha 11 May, Rajya Sabha 12 May 2005; President's assent 15 June 2005; in force 12 October 2005 (after 120 days); a legal right.
